2608.05993.title: Clinical Communication Processing with Models Trained on LLM-Generated Synthetic Data: A Structured Survey and Novel Application Case Studies
2608.05993.paper_summary: Much clinical value is conveyed not through structured records but through communication: exchanges in which patients describe symptoms, clinicians reason and give instructions, ambulances hand over to emergency departments, and nurses pass on a shift. Such language differs from tabular data because meaning depends on speaker role, intent, causality, uncertainty, omission, and channel noise. Healthcare natural language processing must therefore interpret information as conveyed rather than coded. This requires well-annotated corpora, which are scarce because authentic exchanges are private, fragmented, and costly to annotate. Large language models offer a way forward by transforming clinical sources, such as records, diagnostic labels, symptom lists, or care plans, into written and transcribed communication for downstream models. We present a structured narrative survey organized by source representation, communication form and participants, generation method, and downstream task, complemented by thirteen novel case studies. These build clinical NLP systems for communication channels and languages without labeled real-world data, including EMS pre-arrival reports, field-radio casualty documentation, nurse handoffs, patient-portal triage, and low-resource discharge communication. They show that synthetic communication can bootstrap such systems. Findings include the competitiveness of fine-tuned encoder models over evaluated zero-shot baselines and the value of deliberately degraded communication for robustness. The main limitation is that most studies evaluate on held-out synthetic communication, while train-on-synthetic, test-on-authentic evidence remains limited. We conclude that syn-thetic clinical communication is becoming a practical research resource; establishing it as reusable clinical infrastructure will require authentic-data transfer, safety and external validation.
2608.05993.paper_summary_zh: 許多臨床價值並不是通過結構化記錄傳達的，而是通過交流：患者描述症狀、臨床醫生推理並給出指示、救護車將病人交接給急診部門，以及護士交接班的過程。這種語言與表格數據不同，因為其意義依賴於說話者的角色、意圖、因果關係、不確定性、省略和通道噪音。因此，醫療保健自然語言處理必須解釋所傳達的信息，而不是編碼的信息。這需要良好標註的語料庫，但由於真實的交流是私密的、片段化的，且標註成本高，因此這類語料庫非常稀缺。大型語言模型提供了一種前進的方向，通過將臨床來源（例如記錄、診斷標籤、症狀列表或護理計劃）轉化為書面和轉錄的交流，以供下游模型使用。我們提出了一個結構化的敘事調查，根據來源表示、交流形式和參與者、生成方法和下游任務進行組織，並輔以十三個新案例研究。這些研究建立了針對通訊渠道和語言的臨床NLP系統，而無需標註的真實世界數據，包括EMS到達前報告、現場無線電傷亡文檔、護士交接、患者門戶分診和低資源出院交流。它們顯示合成交流可以啟動這些系統。研究結果包括微調編碼器模型在評估的零樣本基準上具有競爭力，以及故意降級的交流對穩健性的價值。主要的限制是大多數研究在保留的合成交流上進行評估，而在合成數據上訓練、在真實證據上測試的情況仍然有限。我們得出結論，合成臨床交流正成為一種實用的研究資源；將其建立為可重用的臨床基礎設施將需要真實數據的轉移、安全性和外部驗證。
2608.05993.author: Alexander Apartsin et.al.
